references.text: Moses predicted that God would choose one specific place for worship. Jesus points beyond this by saying that worship should be neither on the mountain in Samaria nor in Jerusalem – God’s plan transcends any geographical location ([ref:5 Mos 12:5-14|Deuteronomy 12:5-14]).

At the temple dedication, Solomon acknowledges that even the heavens cannot contain God, let alone a house built by human hands. This points to Jesus’ statement that worship is no longer bound to one physical place ([ref:1 Kong 8:27-30|1 Kings 8:27-30]).
The psalmist calls for worship at God’s holy mountain in Jerusalem. Jesus says this location-bound worship will be replaced by something new ([ref:Sal 99:9|Psalms 99:9]).

Isaiah prophesies that all nations will stream to the Lord’s mountain. Jesus expands this perspective: worship of the Father is no longer tied to a specific mountain or city ([ref:Jes 2:2-3|Isaiah 2:2-3]).

Malachi prophesies that the Lord’s name will be great among the nations, and offerings will be made to His name everywhere. This points to a universal worship not bound to Jerusalem ([ref:Mal 1:11|Malachi 1:11]).
Jesus elaborates in the following verses on what this new worship entails: worshipping the Father in spirit and truth, independent of geographical location ([ref:Joh 4:23-24|John 4:23-24]).

Jesus speaks of His body as the new temple that will be raised in three days. This supports His words that worship is no longer bound to the physical temple in Jerusalem ([ref:Joh 2:19-21|John 2:19-21]).

Stephen quotes the prophet Isaiah and proclaims that the Most High does not dwell in houses made by human hands, confirming Jesus’ words that worship is not bound to a specific place ([ref:Apg 7:48-50|Acts 7:48-50]).
Paul urges men everywhere to pray and lift up holy hands – worship is no longer limited to Jerusalem or any other specific location ([ref:1 Tim 2:8|1 Timothy 2:8]).

The letter to the Hebrews explains that the old sanctuary and its arrangements were a shadow of something greater. Christ entered heaven itself as our high priest, making the role of the earthly temple obsolete ([ref:Hebr 9:8-12|Hebrews 9:8-12]).
